sections.h2: Which office collects Suffolk County property tax?
sections.html:
There is no single county tax office for current bills. Ten town Receivers of Taxes (Babylon, Brookhaven, East Hampton, Huntington, Islip, Riverhead, Shelter Island, Smithtown, Southampton and Southold) send and collect one combined bill that covers town, school and county levies. They take payments from December 1 through May 31. Whatever is still open after that date moves to the County Comptroller. Value is set by the Assessor in your own town, and the Receiver in that town issues the bill.

The Comptroller's collection office sits at 330 Center Drive, Riverhead, NY 11901. Staff are in from 9:00 a.m. until five, but the payment counter shuts at 4:15 p.m. Call 631-852-3000 for the main line.

  • Town Receiver of Taxes: bills, duplicates and payments up to May 31.
  • Town Assessor: value, exemptions and a new mailing address.
  • County Comptroller: delinquent tax, bankruptcies, refunds of overpayment, tax liens and redemption statements.

Other levies can ride on the same bill. Your Receiver can tell you which ones apply to your parcel.

The tax year starts December 1 and ends the next November 30. Receivers mail bills around mid-December. Pay half by January 10 and you owe no interest on it. Pay it later and interest of 1 percent a month builds on that half until May 31. The other half can be paid with no interest at any point through May 31.

Two things catch buyers and sellers in spring. First, a person who buys during the year needs to learn whether the second-half tax is already paid, because the new owner inherits the problem. Second, a military-service or senior exemption belongs to the person who earned it. It stops at the sale, and the buyer's first bill can be far higher than yours.

You may pay in installments as small as $200, either to the Receiver or to the Comptroller. Penalties and interest then run only on what is left. Taking a partial payment does not release the County's lien on the rest.

An open balance turns delinquent and is owed to the County Comptroller. A 5 percent penalty applies, and interest of 1 percent a month is counted from February 1 on the tax plus the penalty. If anything is still unpaid after August 31, a tax sale advertising fee is added. This table gives the total interest by the month you pay.

Interest added to delinquent Suffolk County tax by month of payment
Month paidInterest rate
June5%
July6%
August7%
September8%
October9%
November10%
December11%

Send a delinquent payment by mail to the Comptroller at the Riverhead address above. Copy the property description word for word from your bill or deed. The percentage climbs every month, so a seller with a late balance saves money by closing sooner.

sections.h2: Can the County take your house over unpaid tax?
sections.html:
Not right away. On the lien sale date, normally in November or December, the Comptroller sells the County a tax lien on each parcel that is still unpaid. The list of liens is advertised first, for six weeks in the official newspapers and for two weeks in a paper serving each of the ten towns.

After the sale you can wipe out the lien by applying to the Comptroller and paying the lien amount, the interest that has built up, and any later County taxes. You have twelve months from the sale. A parcel assessed as a one-, two- or three-family home gets thirty-six months. The Comptroller will give you a redemption statement covering every open lien if you ask.

Once the redemption period ends, the County issues a tax deed. To recover property after that, apply to the Suffolk County Department of Planning, Division of Real Estate, at 631-853-5900.

sections.h2: After you buy a house or pay off a mortgage
sections.html:
Call your local Receiver of Taxes at once. New owners should ask for a current bill and for the next payment date. If you have just paid off a mortgage that carried an escrow account, ask the Receiver to mail future bills to you directly, and confirm the address on file.

  • Ask whether the second-half tax has been paid on the parcel.
  • Ask the Assessor to fix the mailing address, because bills are built from the Assessor's roll.
  • If a mortgage ended partway through the year, find out whether the bank paid the full year. The bank has no duty to forward a bill.
  • Keep paperwork for any exemption you plan to claim by March 1.

The Comptroller's main number, 631-852-3000, also handles refunds of overpaid tax, bankruptcy questions, and court-ordered reductions or corrections of error.

Take your complaint to your town's review board on Grievance Day. That is the third Tuesday in May, or May 18 in 2027. The board has to sit for a minimum of four hours. The yearly assessment calendar goes like this:

  • January 1: valuation date.
  • March 1: taxable status date, and the last day to file any exemption.
  • Third Tuesday in May: Grievance Day.
  • July 1: final roll, with taxes extended from it.

When the board denies relief, you can file a small claims petition within 30 days after the final roll is filed. You must already have a written complaint on file with the Board of Assessment Review, and the home must be a one-, two- or three-family house used only as a residence. The file for your assessment is kept by your town Assessor, so ask there for the property record card and for sales of similar homes before you file.

sections.h2: Suffolk housing and what to gather before listing
sections.html:
Suffolk is a costly, owner-heavy county. Median home value for 2020-2024 is $578,400, and 82.2 percent of homes are lived in by their owners, among 512,565 households. Median gross rent is $2,255. The estimate for July 2025 is 1,546,090 residents.

Much of the housing sits near sea level, so buyers tend to ask about flood and drainage history. Dig out your insurance records and any elevation certificate. Put them in a folder with the current tax bill, your exemption letters, and a redemption statement if a lien was ever sold on the parcel. Give the folder to your closing attorney early. Taxes still open do not stop a cash sale, since the payoff comes out of your proceeds, but you need that payoff figure in writing for the exact closing date. Ask for it early in the month, because interest is added monthly and a closing that slips across a month line changes the number.

faqs.q: Who do I pay Suffolk County property tax to before May 31?
faqs.a: The Receiver of Taxes in your town, from December 1 through May 31. After that the balance is owed to the County Comptroller.

faqs.q: How long can I redeem a Suffolk County tax lien?
faqs.a: Twelve months after the lien sale, or thirty-six months for a one-, two- or three-family home. Once that window closes, the County issues a tax deed.

faqs.q: Is a mailed Suffolk tax payment accepted by postmark?
faqs.a: Yes, if the envelope carries a USPS postmark. A metered postmark does not count, so use certified or registered mail close to a deadline.

faqs.q: What if I never received my Suffolk County tax bill?
faqs.a: You owe the tax anyway, with any penalty and interest. Ask your town Receiver of Taxes for a duplicate right away.

faqs.q: Does a Suffolk tax exemption move to the buyer of my house?
faqs.a: No. A military-service or senior exemption stays with the person who earned it, so the buyer's first tax bill can run higher than yours.
